lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Are you currently responsible for Alex in terms of providing for his care and upbringing? For example, do you pay for things like his food, clothing, and housing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm fully responsible for Alex. I provide for all his needs - his food, clothing, housing, everything really. He lives at home with me and I take care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, I need to ask about your immigration status. Are you a UK citizen, or do you have a different immigration status? If you're not a UK citizen, what is your current immigration status in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, so no issues there with immigration status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask: Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for him? For example, the other parent or another family member?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him, and I haven't claimed it before - that's why I'm checking now if I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just a few more questions to ensure I have all the information needed:

1. Does Alex live with you full-time in the UK, or does he spend time living with anyone else (such as another parent or relative)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He does live with me full-time, but I should mention - he has been in care for a little while. But he still comes home to stay with me regularly, like on weekends and such. So he's not there all the time, he spends quite a bit of time at home with me each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information about Alex's situation.

I need to understand this a bit better. When you say Alex has been "in care," can you clarify what type of care arrangement this is? For example:

- Is he in local authority care (foster care)?
- Is he in a children's home?
- Or is it a different type of arrangement?

And approximately how much time does he spend with you versus in the care placement each week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in local authority care - been there for a few months now. But like I said, he comes home to spend time with me regularly. He's with me quite a bit each week - basically comes home on the weekends and stays with me, so it's more than a full day each week that he's home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details. This is important information for determining eligibility.

I have a few follow-up questions about Alex's care arrangement:

1. While Alex is in local authority care, is the local authority receiving any payments or funding specifically for his care and maintenance?

2. What is the plan for Alex's care - is this a temporary arrangement with a view to him returning to live with you permanently, or is it a longer-term care arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, the local authority is the one looking after him while he's in care - they're providing for his care there. 

As for the arrangement, well, it's been going on for a few months now. He still comes home regularly to be with me, but I'm not sure exactly when or if he'll be back living with me full-time permanently. It's just the current situation we're in.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I understand this must be a difficult situation.

One more important question: Do you contribute financially towards Alex's care and maintenance while he's in the local authority care placement? For example, do you pay any money towards the costs of his care, or do you pay for things like his clothing, pocket money, or other expenses while he's in care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do still contribute financially for Alex. I help out with things he needs - you know, buying him clothes, things for school, that sort of thing. I still make sure he has what he needs even while he's in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me, I need to inform you about the eligibility rules that apply to your situation:

**Unfortunately, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under these circumstances.**

Here's why: When a child is in local authority care and the local authority is maintaining them (providing for their care), Child Benefit cannot be paid to a parent or anyone else for that child - even if the child comes home to visit regularly and even if you contribute financially towards their needs.

The rules state that Child Benefit is not payable for a child who is being looked after by a local authority. This applies regardless of:
- How often Alex comes home to visit you
- The fact that you still contribute financially to his needs
- Whether the care arrangement might be temporary

The local authority would be considered responsible for Alex during the period he is in their care, which makes him ineligible for Child Benefit claims during this time.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future and he returns to live with you full-time (no longer in local authority care), you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that point.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So even though he comes home regularly and I'm still paying for his things, because the local authority has him in care, I can't claim the benefit right now?

Just to be clear - if things change and he does come back to live with me full-time, then I could claim it at that point?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. I can see this is disappointing news, but you've understood the situation correctly.

**Current situation:** Because Alex is in local authority care and the local authority is maintaining him, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him right now - even though you're contributing financially and he visits you regularly on weekends.

**If circumstances change:** If Alex returns to live with you full-time and is no longer in local authority care, then at that point you would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, as long as:
- He's under 16 (or under 20 if in approved education or training)
- You're responsible for him
- He lives with you
- No one else is claiming for him

You would need to make a new claim at that time when he comes back to live with you permanently.

I understand this must be a difficult situation for you and Alex. If his care arrangements do change in the future, don't hesitate to apply for Child Benefit at that time.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, I think that's clear now. Thank you for explaining it to me. It's not what I was hoping to hear, but at least I know where I stand. I'll make sure to apply if Alex does come back home to live with me full-time.

Thanks for your help.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome. I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you, even though it wasn't the news you were hoping for.

You're doing the right thing by staying involved in Alex's life and continuing to support him. I wish you and Alex all the best, and I hope circumstances work out so that he can return home to you.

Take care, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions in the future.
